extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting short/shorter speculative fiction to Strange Horizons
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting speculative fiction (short stories up to ~10,000 words, preference for <5,000) to the online magazine Strange Horizons, including content preferences, formatting, rights, payment, and submission procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculative fiction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We want: Speculative fiction, broadly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your story doesn't have a speculative element, or strong speculative-fiction sensibilities, it's probably not for us.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred and maximum length
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 10,000 words (under 5000 preferred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We prefer stories under 5,000 words, but consider stories up to 10,000 words. The longer the story, the less likely we are to be interested. The wordcount limit is not absolutely inflexible, but we can't consider stories much over the limit. No minimum wordcount requirement; short-short stories are considered. We determine story length by taking the word-processor wordcount and rounding up to the next highest 100 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission gateway and allowed file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted here, via our Moksha submissions system — no email or postal submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In order to track stories correctly, we can only consider stories submitted through that form—no email or paper mail submissions. Please send only RTF, DOC or DOCX files and try to stick to standard manuscript format as much as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous/multiple submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No simultaneous or multiple submissions; no re-submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions sent to us and another venue simultaneously are not allowed. Multiple stories at once from the same author are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous submission / previous publication restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously unpublished in English—we buy first English rights, including audio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will consider stories which have previously appeared in another language, but have never been published in English. We won't consider unsolicited reprints of works previously published in English. Stories previously submitted to Strange Horizons, even if they have been revised, are not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights purchased and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: We buy first-printing world exclusive English-language rights (including audio rights) for six (6) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After that period you are free to republish the story elsewhere. We hope you'll allow us to leave the story in our archives indefinitely after it's rotated off the main table of contents, but you have the right to remove your story from the archives at any time after one (1) year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rate and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay 10¢/word (USD), with a minimum payment of $60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment will be made within 60 days of contract. We pay by check or PayPal, according to the author's preference. SFWA officially considers us a professional market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Your cover letter can be minimal: generally, these should be short and list just a few of your most recent or most relevant publications or workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you've got life experience relevant to your story, please mention it. Cover letters shouldn't include plot synopses or pitches. See the sample cover letters page if concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting and author ID
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to stick to standard manuscript format as much as possible. Along with your name and contact information in the upper left, you may also add your pronouns (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your legal name does not need to be anywhere on your submission; we'll only ask for it for our contract and payment if your story is accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content tastes and special interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Some particular things we love, or are interested in: Fiction from or about diverse perspectives and traditionally under-represented groups, settings, and cultures, written from a non-exoticizing and well-researched position; unusual yet readable styles and inventive structures and narratives; stories that address political issues in complex and nuanced ways, resisting oversimplification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypertext fiction, interactive fiction, and other stories that explore and exploit the forms available to us are of interest—query to discuss how to submit such works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable content boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Things which are fine: Profanity is fine. Use whatever words are appropriate for your story. Sex or violence in a story should be artistically justified; no excessive gore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We welcome submissions from anywhere in the world, and British spellings are fine. We welcome all subgenres and forms of speculative fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disallowed submission types and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Things which we won't consider: Stories above 10,000 words, including serialized novels or novellas; partial or incomplete stories; unsolicited reprints of works previously published in English; stories previously submitted to Strange Horizons; multiple stories at once from the same author; submissions sent to us and another venue simultaneously; poetry or nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please don't send part of a story and ask us to request the rest later. Serialized novels/novellas and partial/incomplete works are not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations routing and relationship to Samovar
rubrics_metrics.description: Special note on translations: our quarterly sister magazine Samovar specializes in translations: we encourage you to submit all translations there first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samovar and Strange Horizons have independent submissions queues and different editors, and submissions to either magazine are only read for that magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive/hypertext submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypertext fiction, interactive fiction, and other stories that explore and exploit the forms available to us—please query us to discuss how to submit it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Querying first allows editorial discussion of format and how best to submit non-standard digital/interactive work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autoresponse and tracking requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We send an autoresponder message in response to every submission we receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you haven't received an autoresponse within 24 hours after submitting, please query immediately. Missing an autoresponse usually means we have an incorrect email address for you and won't be able to contact you when we make a decision on your fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query/contact protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have any questions, write to fiction@strangehorizons.com with the word QUERY: at the beginning of your subject line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you don't get a response within a month to your email, please query again. If you're having trouble submitting, or have any other questions, include 'QUERY: Your Question Topic' as subject and contact that address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: After you submit a story, we strongly prefer you don't withdraw it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you withdraw a story, we won't consider any version of that story in the future. If you do need to withdraw a story, please send an e-mail telling us that you need to withdraw, and let us know why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive retention and author removal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: We hope you'll allow us to leave the story in our archives indefinitely after it's rotated off the main table of contents, but you have the right to remove your story from the archives at any time after one (1) year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain the option to remove archived stories after the one-year period despite the magazine's preference to keep them online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wordcount rounding and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: We determine story length by taking the word-processor wordcount and rounding up to the next highest 100 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the method Strange Horizons uses to decide whether a submission fits their length thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: No email/postal submissions or alternative file types
rubrics_metrics.description: We can only consider stories submitted through the Moksha submission gateway; no email or paper mail submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only RTF, DOC, or DOCX are accepted. Non-standard formats or sending via email will not be considered.
